title: Aubergine settings
description: config.json in the data folder of an Aubergine server. Every key may be left out; what is left out takes its default.

$schema.description: Where an editor finds this schema: "./config.schema.json". Aubergine itself does not read it.

family.default: Menlo, Monaco, "DejaVu Sans Mono", Consolas, monospace
family.description: The fonts of a terminal’s text, as a CSS font-family list: the first one found is used.

size.description: The size of a terminal’s text, in pixels.

theme.description: Light, dark, or whichever the system is set to (`system`), following it when that changes.

appearance.description: How the page looks beyond light or dark: the color theme of each, a terminal’s theme and cursor, and colors set by hand.

light.description: The color theme drawn when the page is light: a built-in one of that kind, or the ID of a theme file of that kind.

dark.description: The color theme drawn when the page is dark: a built-in one of that kind, or the ID of a theme file of that kind.

cursor.description: The shape of a terminal’s cursor.

terminal.description: The color theme of every terminal that has none of its own, of either kind, built-in or of a theme file. Null: the theme the page is drawn in.

byTag.description: Color themes for terminals by tag, in order: a terminal that has no theme of its own is drawn in the theme of the first entry whose tag it has (whatever the capitals) and whose theme is there now. At most 20. A wrong entry is skipped and the rest still count.

tag.description: A terminal’s tag, as tags are written: whatever the capitals, the same tag.

theme.description: The color theme of the terminals with that tag, of either kind, built-in or of a theme file.

titleFormat.description: What a terminal’s title says after its name, on the canvas and at the head of a terminal in a browser tab of its own: a template, text with placeholders such as {state} and {folder} (see docs/templates.md). One line, at most 200 characters. A placeholder that is not known is skipped; a template that is wrong as a whole is the default.

rowFormat.description: What a terminal’s row in the list says on its second line: a template, as `titleFormat` is (see docs/templates.md). Compact, a row has no second line and says its state alone. One line, at most 200 characters.

customCss.description: Whether your own stylesheet, `custom.css` in the data folder, is linked on the page when there is one (docs/custom-css.md). Off: the page is drawn without it, as with `?plain` after its address.

colors.description: Colors set by hand over the theme that is drawn: `"<color>": "#rrggbb"` for every theme, or `"[<theme id>]": { … }` for one theme alone (built-in or of a theme file), which wins. Written by hand only.

[light].description: Colors set by hand for Light alone, over those for every theme.

[high-contrast-light].description: Colors set by hand for High contrast light alone, over those for every theme.

[solarized-light].description: Colors set by hand for Solarized light alone, over those for every theme.

[gruvbox-light].description: Colors set by hand for Gruvbox light alone, over those for every theme.

[dark].description: Colors set by hand for Dark alone, over those for every theme.

[high-contrast-dark].description: Colors set by hand for High contrast dark alone, over those for every theme.

[solarized-dark].description: Colors set by hand for Solarized dark alone, over those for every theme.

[gruvbox-dark].description: Colors set by hand for Gruvbox dark alone, over those for every theme.

[nord].description: Colors set by hand for Nord alone, over those for every theme.

[dracula].description: Colors set by hand for Dracula alone, over those for every theme.

^\\[[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}\\]$.description: Colors set by hand for a theme of your own (a file in themes/ in the data folder) alone, over those for every theme.

shell.description: The whole path of the shell new terminals start. Null: your own `$SHELL`.

defaultFolder.description: The folder new terminals start in (`~` may begin it). Null: the home folder.

away.description: What changed while you were away.

afterMinutes.description: After this many minutes without the page being looked at, coming back shows what changed meanwhile. 0 switches that off.

logPrompts.description: Keep the prompts given to agents in the terminal’s note log. Turn this off if prompts may hold secrets.

claudeCommand.description: The command line that starts Claude Code. It may be a whole launcher, such as `mytool launch -- claude`; Aubergine’s own flags are added at the end, or where `{flags}` is.

api.description: Limits on calls made with API tokens. They apply from the next start of the server.

rateLimitPerMinute.description: How many calls one API token may make in a minute.

maxBodyBytes.description: The largest request body the server takes, in bytes.

activityLogMaxBytes.description: How large the activity log may grow before its older half is dropped, in bytes.

workflows.description: Limits on workflows, and when a run counts as quiet.

maxElements.description: How many steps one workflow may have.

maxElementChars.description: How long the text of one step (or the text for every step) may be, in characters.

quietAfterSeconds.description: A running run is marked quiet when its terminal has printed for this many seconds after the last report.

library.description: The library: how long and how much a fetch of a Git source may take. They apply from the next start of the server.

fetchTimeoutSeconds.description: The longest one Git command of a refresh may run, in seconds.

maxFetchMegabytes.description: The largest file Git may write while fetching, in megabytes: a source that needs more is refused.

messages.description: Messages between terminals: how many, how often, and when a thread waits for the owner. They apply from the next start of the server.

perSenderPerMinute.description: How many messages one sender may send in a minute, to anyone.

perPairPerHour.description: How many messages may pass between the same two in an hour, both ways together.

pauseAfter.description: After this many messages between two that are not the owner, without the owner having looked, the thread pauses.

maxUnread.description: How many unread messages a terminal may have waiting. One more is refused.

nudgeIntervalSeconds.description: The fixed sentence that says a message is waiting is not typed into the same terminal again within this many seconds.

keepDays.description: Read messages older than this many days are left out of what is listed.

logMaxBytes.description: How large the file of messages may grow before its older part is set aside, in bytes.

describe.description: What a terminal says about itself.

remind.description: Whether an agent that stops with its terminal not named, or with no summary, is told once to set them.

pullRequests.description: Whether the pull request of a terminal’s branch is asked of the `gh` tool, where that is installed and signed in.

desktop.description: Opening a canvas terminal in your own terminal application.

app.description: Which application opens a terminal on the desktop: `terminal` or `iterm` (macOS), or `command` for a command line of your own. Null: the usual one for this system, `terminal` on macOS, and `command` elsewhere once one is written.

command.description: For `command`: the command line, with `{file}` where the script file goes. It is started without a shell.

openNew.description: New terminals made in the page also open on the desktop.

lateWithinHours.description: A time that passed while the server was stopped or the computer asleep still runs, marked late, when it is at most this many hours old; older, it is missed. 0: never late. It applies from the next start of the server.

terminal.description: Terminal access for programs with an API token: what is people only from the start, the limits, and the audit of typed text.

protectNewSessions.description: New terminals are “people only” from the start.

protectAgentSessions.description: New terminals that start an agent are “people only” from the start: a token typing into an agent is the riskiest case.

inputCallsPerMinute.description: How many input calls one token may make to one terminal in a minute.

inputCharsPerCall.description: How many characters one input call may carry.

inputCharsPerMinute.description: How many characters one token may type into one terminal in a minute.

maxWaitingRuns.description: How many commands may be waited for at once, over all terminals.

auditInput.description: Keep the text that tokens type, itself, in `input.log` in the data folder. Off: only its length and a fingerprint are recorded.

access.description: Reaching this server from another device or page. Written by hand only; a wrong entry is reported and skipped.

addresses.description: HTTPS origins this server also answers under, through something on this computer that carries HTTPS to it. Read when the server starts.

pages.description: Origins of the pages of another Aubergine that may show this server. Read when the server starts.

shortcuts.description: Keys: a command’s name to a chord (`"Ctrl+Meta+J"`), a list of chords, or null for no key. A wrong entry is reported and skipped.

on.description: Which plugins (folders in plugins/ in the data folder) run in the page, as you: a plugin’s ID to the digest it had when you switched it on, or "follow" to run whatever is in its folder. A plugin whose files changed since is not loaded until it is switched on again. A wrong entry is reported and skipped.

^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,39}$.description: The digest the plugin had when it was switched on, or "follow".
